Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot:--his lot be, cast lots, obtain.
BiblicalUsage: To obtain by lot is the word for what falls to a person by God's allotment. In Luke 1:9 Zechariah's "lot was to burn incense" in the temple, in Acts 1:17 Judas "had obtained part of this ministry," and in 2 Peter 1:1 believers "have obtained like precious faith with us."
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that what strikes me is the word's three lots are the whole story of providence: a priest's lot, an apostle's lot, and a faith obtained, and each one fell where God put it.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; Zechariah, Father of John the Baptist
